title: v1-chat-compat-shim-stable-stream-handshake-toolcall-delivery-stop-normalizer
author: Priya Patel
description: Motivation: Close remaining gaps between Redwood's chat streaming surface and OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics to improve compatibility for customers migrating from OpenAI and to stabilize function/toolcall delivery in intermittent network scenarios. This PR implements a compact handshake + heartbeat for stream sessions, formalizes a toolcall delivery envelope to ensure deterministic ordering across reconnects, and normalizes 'stop' token handling and logprobs propagation to match OpenAI expectations. Changes are backwards-compatible by default via a feature flag (OPENAI_V1_COMPAT=off). Checklist: [x] streaming handshake frame with version negotiation and optional heartbeat interval; [x] idempotent resume protocol that replays in-flight toolcall events but deduplicates based on server-generated event ids; [x] stop-token normalizer that accepts single string or array inputs and converts to runtime stop predicates; [x] logprobs envelope mapping preserved for both token and token_offset semantics; [x] added E2E tests that simulate reconnects and reordered packets; [x] docs and SDK examples updated. Impact: reduces dropped tool/function calls during transient disconnects, prevents duplicate tool invocations on resume, and brings Redwood's response shape into parity with common OpenAI clients (roles, message-ids, stop arrays). Rollout: gated behind feature flag; staged rollout to Dedicated customers first, then hosted; can be disabled at runtime per-tenant. Related: Linear ENG-2345 (stream stability), PM-412 (compat parity), Jira SUP-987 (customer incident reproduction). Migration notes: customers using custom stream consumers must minor-update framing parsing (new initial JSON handshake event with "compat_version"); SDKs updated to handle both old and new envelopes. CI: new unit and integration tests added; flaky test allowance adjusted for reconnect timings.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add stream handshake frame and heartbeat negotiation
fix(streaming): deterministic toolcall envelope and resume/dedupe logic
feat(api): accept stop as string or array and normalize at adapter layer
test(streaming): e2e reconnect scenarios for toolcall ordering
docs(openai-compat): examples for new handshake and resume semantics
release_notes: Add OpenAI /v1 chat compatibility: streaming handshake + heartbeat, deterministic toolcall envelope with resume/dedupe, and stop-token normalization. Feature gated; off by default. Refer to docs/openai-compat.md for migration steps.
review_comments: Alex Chen: Nice work on the resume logic; two questions: can you walk through a timeline where server assigns event ids and client resends stale frames? Also please add a metric for resume-replays.

Author (Priya Patel): Responded: server now assigns stable event ids on accept; client keeps local provisional ids until ack and resume compares server ids for dedupe. I added 'stream.resume_replays' counter and included it in metrics dashboard updates.
Miguel Torres: Integration test looks good; please add a negative test that simulates duplicate toolcall payloads arriving after resume.
Author: Added a negative-e2e that injects duplicated toolcall on reconnect and assert single invocation; test included in e2e suite and passes.
Sofia Martinez: Docs clarification: how does this interact with existing prefix/KV cache? Could resume deliver tokens already in cache? Consider noting expected behavior.

Author: Added docs note: resume only replays toolcall control events and message metadata; token stream resumes from last acknowledged token and cache keys are not retransmitted. Updated openai-compat.md.

Integration: adjusted streaming test harness to simulate TCP disconnects and reordered packets
E2E: reconnect_toolcall_test.go simulates 3 reconnect cycles and asserts idempotent tool invocation
